title: Docker Socket Compatibility warning after upgrading Podman Desktop on Windows 11
body: After upgrading Podman Desktop to v1.2.1 on Windows 11, I get the warning: “Docker Socket Compatibility: Docker socket is not reachable. Docker specific tools may not work.” The logs show missing Docker and Podman named pipes, including ENOENT for //./pipe/docker_engine and \\.\pipe\podman-machine-default, while Podman Desktop says a machine is already starting or started.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Podman Desktop 1.2.1 on Windows 11, I see “Docker Socket Compatibility: Docker socket is not reachable. Docker specific tools may not work.”
The logs show ENOENT errors for the Docker and default Podman machine pipes even though Podman Desktop says a machine is already starting or started.
N0.label: N0 socket warning reported

symptoms_visible: The Docker socket warning remains, and Docker Desktop is not installed on my machine.
N1_x.label: N1_x Docker Desktop restart direction rejected

symptoms_visible: The Docker socket warning remains; Docker Desktop is not installed, and I can list many Windows named pipes.
N1.label: N1 named pipes inspected

symptoms_visible: I cannot stop the default Podman machine normally, and removing it says the running VM cannot be destroyed.
Running podman info fails because the TCP connection to the local Podman service is actively refused.
N2.label: N2 machine marked running but unreachable

symptoms_visible: After forcibly terminating the WSL machine, I could remove the Podman machine, but creating it again failed.
Process Explorer did not find docker_engine or podman-machine handles.
N3_x.label: N3_x forced removal followed by failed initialization

symptoms_visible: After following the linked WSL troubleshooting article, I no longer see the earlier problem and report that it appears resolved.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved after WSL remediation

solution.intent: Quit Docker Desktop, stop the Podman machine, quit Podman Desktop, and then reopen Podman Desktop and restart the machine so Podman can take the Docker pipe.
solution.concrete_example: With Podman Desktop open, quit Docker Desktop from its tray icon, stop the Podman machine, quit Podman Desktop, reopen it, and start the machine.

edges.comment: From c6-c7, on the reporter's system: the proposed Docker Desktop shutdown sequence is inapplicable because the reporter states that Docker Desktop is not installed.

question_patterns: Is Docker Desktop installed or running on this machine?
Could another Docker installation currently own the Docker named pipe?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Docker Desktop is not installed on my machine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Docker Desktop is installed and running, and it owns the docker_engine pipe.

question_patterns: Can you run dir \\.\pipe\ in PowerShell and paste the full named-pipe list?
Please run [System.IO.Directory]::GetFiles("\\.\\pipe\\") and share its raw output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: There are a lot of entries. GetFiles by itself was not recognized, but dir \\.\pipe\ worked, so I pasted the output after removing duplicate lines.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The list includes active docker_engine and podman-machine-default pipes.
The same pipe list was produced with the fully qualified GetFiles command instead of dir.

edges.comment: From c2-c7, on the reporter's Windows 11 system: maintainers request the raw pipe listing, and the reporter also clarifies that Docker Desktop is absent.

question_patterns: Since Docker Desktop is not installed, can you list the current Windows named pipes with dir \\.\pipe\ and paste the output?
Can you provide the full named-pipe list so we can check what the container engine exposed?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran dir \\.\pipe\ and pasted the long result after removing duplicate lines.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both docker_engine and podman-machine-default are present and usable in the list.

edges.comment: Recovery from the rejected c6 direction using the actual c2-c7 diagnostic request on the same reporter's system. The image was already attached to the canonical equivalent edge and is not reused.

question_patterns: Can you stop all Podman machines, start the default machine from the CLI, and then check the pipes again?
What happens when you try to stop and restart the default Podman machine?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am unable to stop the Podman machine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The machine stops and starts normally, and both expected pipes appear afterward.

question_patterns: If the machine remains stuck, what raw output do you get from podman machine rm?
Can the default Podman machine be removed and recreated?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: podman machine rm returns: Error: running vm "podman-machine-default" cannot be destroyed.

question_patterns: What does podman info return while the machine claims to be running?
Can the Podman CLI contact the service?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: podman info fails with: Error: failed to connect: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:56107: connectex: No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: podman info succeeds and prints normal host and engine information.
The same connection-refused error uses a different ephemeral localhost port.

edges.comment: From c8-c15, solely on the opening reporter's system: attempts to stop, inspect, and remove the default machine establish the raw contradiction that it is marked running but cannot be contacted.

solution.intent: Force-terminate the stuck WSL Podman machine, check for stale pipe handles, and then remove and recreate the Podman machine.
solution.concrete_example: Run wsl --terminate podman-machine-default, search Process Explorer for docker_engine and podman-machine handles, then run podman machine rm, podman machine init, and podman machine start.

edges.comment: From c16-c17, on the reporter's system: forced WSL termination and machine removal succeed, but Process Explorer finds no relevant handles and podman machine init fails, so this sequence alone does not resolve the case.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as a broken WSL/Podman VM state rather than Docker Desktop pipe contention, apply the remediation from the linked WSL troubleshooting article, and have the reporter verify Podman Desktop afterward.
solution.concrete_example: Because the VM is marked running but cannot be contacted and a fresh machine cannot be initialized, follow the suggested WSL troubleshooting article, then reopen Podman Desktop and confirm that the original socket warning and machine failure are gone.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied only the observed machine, pipe, connection, and initialization failures. Localizing the fault to the WSL-backed Podman VM state, rather than to Docker Desktop or the UI warning itself, is the engineer's inference from that evidence.

edges.comment: From c18-c19, on the opening reporter's system: the maintainer points to a WSL troubleshooting article without describing its internal steps, and the reporter follows it, posts new screenshots, and says the issue appears resolved. Later comments from other users are not spliced into this reporter's resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted diagnosis at the level established by the thread: the Docker socket warning is downstream of a broken or stuck WSL-backed Podman machine state that is marked running but cannot be contacted or recreated normally.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: missing pipe connection behavior, inability to stop the machine, podman info receiving a localhost connection refusal, and podman machine init failing after forced termination and removal.
Must not recommend quitting Docker Desktop as the resolution because Docker Desktop is not installed on the reporter's machine.
Must not claim that force-terminating and running podman machine rm/init/start alone fixed the issue; removal succeeded, but initialization then failed.

Must direct the reporter to the linked WSL troubleshooting remediation without inventing undocumented steps from that external article, and must ask the reporter to verify that the warning and machine failure are gone before declaring resolution.

persona_hint.experience_level: Windows user comfortable running copied PowerShell, Podman CLI, WSL, and Process Explorer instructions, but not independently diagnosing named pipes or VM internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief, cooperative, and evidence-oriented; pastes exact command errors and screenshots, and reports outcomes directly.
